ask: provision for doubtful debts
why: the provision column, its rate, or its range; 'doubtful' is not a word the sheet uses

ask: what rate is each debt discounted at
why: the rate column, the table it is looked up in, or either's range

ask: present value of what is owed
why: the discounted column or its range

ask: how long has each account been overdue
why: the raw count of days or the bucket it falls in

ask: ageing buckets
why: the column of bucket labels

ask: what rate applies to each type of debtor
why: the lookup relation: debt type keys into the rates table, and an agent may name the formula that does it

ask: impairment
why: the single word the whole workbook is named for

ask: total balance outstanding
why: an agent should give the figure or the cell that totals it; the column name alone is the retrieval-level answer

ask: notes on how the calculation works
why: the sheet of prose; explaining the formulas instead is not what was asked

ask: what was billed in january
why: the January sheet, or the summary line that sums the quarter

ask: tax rate
why: the defined name, the cell it names, or its value

ask: which territory is an account in
why: the territory column

ask: percentage provided against each band of days
why: the banding table on the rates sheet

ask: account number
why: the key column

ask: which accounts are in Ironwood
why: the territory column, or the count of rows in it
a figure the index cannot hold: the cell that stores it, the summary cell that computes it as a maximum, or the column
a figure in the middle of a large numeric column, found only by scanning cells; the retrieval scorer records this as a known gap, and an agent with `find_value` closes it

ask: what is the total present value of everything owed
why: no cell holds this: it is a sum over the Present Value column, which only `query_table` can produce

ask: how much is owed in total by accounts in Ironwood
why: a filtered sum: `query_table` where Territory is Ironwood, sum of Balance

ask: how many accounts are business debt
why: a filtered count over the Debt Type column

ask: which formula computes each account's provision
why: the formula text of the provision column, from `read_cells` or `precedents`; any row's instance is right

ask: what provision percentage applies to a debt more than 120 days overdue
why: the last band of the rates table, or the sentence in the notes that states it

ask: if the tax rate were 20 percent, what would the provision after tax be
why: a what-if: change Tax_Rate (Rates!B11) to 0.2 and read Summary!B11, which `what_if` reports as moved
